title: stepscroll tiles
description: Every tile a page of the world can hold, keyed by the tile's name. A page is 256 pixels across and 256 lines down. A tile is a list of pieces in Cyberun's form (examples/jetrun/world/tiles.schema.json), drawn with Cyberun's own step graphics: straight runs of identical steps. Rock is decided down each world column: sky above the world, turned by every floor or ceiling crossed, so sky and solid rock are tiles with no pieces. A tile may instead be another tile drawn mirrored or upside down, Cyberun's way. See world.py and cyberun_steps.py.

from.description: The tile whose pieces this one draws.

mirrored.description: Drawn mirrored left to right, Cyberun's $FF marker.

upsideDown.description: Drawn upside down, Cyberun's $99 marker: floors become ceilings in place.

x.description: The left edge of the piece's lowest step, in pixels from the page's left edge (a multiple of 8).

y.description: The bottom line of the piece's lowest step in the page: odd, as the blitters go up a row pair at a time.

direction.description: Cyberun's sixteen: flat steps 24 pixels long, gentle slopes 16 across and 8 up, plain ones 8 and 8, steep ones 8 and 16, walls 16 high. Floors have rock below, ceilings rock above; 'up' climbs to the right, 'down' climbs to the left.

ends.description: Flat pieces only: Cyberun's end codes for the run's first and last steps (bit 4: draw an end cap, the low two bits which; $16: only the last step's first column).
